transcript.text: I scaled a business from here to here
fast. So, this is the business's numbers
beforehand. So, every 100 appointments
booked, 49% of people were showing up,
and out of those, 83% were actually
being offered, and out of those, only
27% closed. And from that, only 47%
paid. And so, the units sold the prior
month in this business was 56. This
business had five problems that we had
to solve. So, problem number one was
show up rate. So, they were optimizing
for the lowest cost leads and
appointments. So, we had them hire a new
media buyer and adjust optimization
towards lowest cost per sale rather than
per lead. Also, we had their setters go
from doing this to doing this. Number
two was close rate. It was too low. So,
during the discovery at the beginning of
the sales call, they were asking service
level questions. So, we optimized the
sales script and helped them create more
questions to really understand why the
prospect was there, so they could have
sell them easier, and then ultimately
get them less objections in the close at
the end of the sale. Number three was
the people and org structure. So, their
team had three parts: sales manager,
closers, and setters. Number one, the
sales manager. The CEO was the sales
manager. He's a great closer, but not a
great sales manager. So, we hired a
sales director who'd been a sales
trainer for a similar type sale before.
Number two, closers. We reduced the
closing team because they had too many.
And so, we cut the lowest percentage
sales people on the team, and we kept
the best ones. Number three was setters.
So, we downsized the setting team and
increased expectations because the
setters' expectations were way too low.
After implementing all these changes,
here were the results.
